After a little heat, regarding what pertains to silver, provided it is also informed with the form of silver, it can turn into gold more easily than from other metals, unless it is deprived of its heat or its natural operation is taken away from it. But if the power of a greater natural heat reaches this quicksilver before it is formed to its end, that is, into the form of silver, so that it is reduced into a pure and red sulfur of Nature, then gold is made from it more quickly than silver, and it remains in it perpetually, which is the end to which nature tends by working.

Quicksilver, which we mentioned just now, is the mother of all metals because of its coldness and humidity. If it becomes pure and separated from every superfluity, then no further coarseness can be mixed with it, such that it would be reduced back into some imperfect metal. For Nature does not work backward, nor is there matter that looks toward some impure form, such as imperfect metals are. But sulfur is the father of all metals because of its heat and dryness. According to this difference, it should be observed that quicksilver is described in the following chapter.

## CHAPTER II.

**T**here is, therefore, in all metals a true <term>Mercurius</term> <gloss>mercury/quicksilver</gloss> and a true sulfur, equally in imperfect as in perfect metals. It has merely been contaminated and rendered impure in imperfect metals, which are deprived of perfect maturation only. And for the same reasons they can be reduced to gold and silver, that is, by separating the impurity with which they had been polluted from the golden or silver nature that is in them, and by infusing into them the form of gold or silver. For they were torn away from nature because they were removed and excavated from natural passages, ores, and veins of the earth; therefore, they can no longer have any operation in themselves, as if they were still lying hidden under the earth. Nevertheless, they desire to be perfected, as much as lies within them.
